summary: Moritz Abraham Stern studied at Heidelberg and the University of Göttingen under Carl Friedrich Gauss and Karl Otfried Müller. In the fields of linguistics and other areas, he held a post as Extraordinarius at Göttingen from 1829 to 1884.

An Indologist, Moritz Spitzer studied at the University of Vienna and completed his Ph.D. at Kiel University under Friedrich Otto Schrader. He served as an assistant at Humboldt University of Berlin from 1927 to 1928.

Working in linguistics and other fields, Moritz Steinschneider studied under Franz Bopp and Heinrich Leberecht Fleischer, earning a PhD from Leipzig. His career included posts at Ephraim Veitel Stiftung, Royal Danish Library, and Jüdische Mädchenschule Berlin.

Moriz Haupt studied under Gottfried Hermann at the University of Leipzig, where he was a Privatdozent, professor extraordinarius, and ordentlicher Professor. In linguistics and other fields, he later served at Humboldt University of Berlin and the Prussian Academy of Sciences.

Moriz Winternitz studied at Vienna under Georg Bühler and under Friedrich Max Müller. In Indology and Buddhist studies, he held positions at Oxford, Visva-Bharati University, and the German University in Prague, where he was Extraordinary Professor (1902–1934).

Linguist Morris Swadesh studied at the University of Chicago under Leonard Bloomfield and Yale University under Edward Sapir. He held faculty posts at Wisconsin-Madison, City College of New York, the National Autonomous University of Mexico, and the University of Alberta.

Morten Schlütter, a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology, studied at Copenhagen, Komazawa, and Yale under Stanley Weinstein, Birthe Arendrup, and Shudo Ishii. He taught at Victoria University of Wellington, UCLA, and the University of Iowa.

Mortimer Wheeler was an archaeologist and Indologist educated at University College London and the University of London. He directed the National Museum Cardiff, the Museum of London, and the Archaeological Survey of India (1944–1948), later teaching at London.

Morton Klass studied at Brooklyn College and Columbia University, where he also studied under Conrad M. Arensberg. Working in religious studies and Indology, he held professorships at Barnard College and Columbia University from approximately 1965 to 1997.

A scholar of linguistics and Indology, Morton W. Easton earned degrees from Yale, including a Ph.D. under William Dwight Whitney, and Columbia. He was a professor at the University of Tennessee (1871–1881) and the University of Pennsylvania (1882–1912).
Active in Buddhist and religious studies, Mother Sayamagyi studied as a disciple under Sayagyi U Ba Khin and eventually succeeded him.

Motohiro Yoritomi, an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar, earned his degrees at Kyoto University, studying under Gadjin Nagao, Yuichi Kajiyama, and Motoshin Yoritomi. He was a professor at Shuchiin University and the Graduate University for Advanced Studies.

Motoi Ono specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied under Yasunori Ejima at the University of Tsukuba and earned his Dr.phil. at the University of Vienna, later becoming an associate professor at Tsukuba around 1996.
Moumita Hossain works in history, archaeology, and Indology. She studied under doctoral supervisor Ranjit Sen and serves as a research scholar/fellow at The Asiatic Society (attested 2026).

Mountstuart Elphinstone, an Indology and history scholar educated at the Royal High School, served with the East India Company, at the Court of the Peshwa, and as envoy and resident before serving as Governor of Bombay (1819–1827).

Mrinal Kaul studied at Delhi, Oxford, and Concordia under Dinanath Yaksha. Active in Indology and philosophy, he taught at the University of Naples, Manipal Academy of Higher Education, and Indian Institute of Technology Bombay.
Working in Indology and philosophy, Mrinalkanti Gangopadhyaya served as a professor at Vidyasagar College in the 1970s and as a lecturer in the Department of Sanskrit at the University of Calcutta.

Mudagamuwe Maithrimurthi completed his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen. Working in Buddhist studies and Indology, he held positions at Leipzig, Heidelberg, and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.
Muhamad Saputra is a PhD student at the Australian National University studying under doctoral supervisor Assa Doron (attested 2026).

Muhamed Riyaz Chenganakkattil works in Indology, history, and archaeology. He earned degrees from Darul Huda, Jamia Millia Islamia, and IIT Delhi, later becoming an Early Doc Fellow at IIT Delhi and a postdoctoral fellow at Ghent University in 2024.
